definitions.explanation: A word or phrase that adds information to or limits the meaning of another word. Includes both adjectives (modifying nouns) and adverbs (modifying verbs).

examples.japanese: 「{美|うつく}しい」は{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}だ。
{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}は{被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}の{前|まえ}に{置|お}く。
examples.english: The modifier is placed before the word it modifies.

examples.japanese: {作文|さくぶん}で{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}を{使|つか}いすぎると、{文|ぶん}がわかりにくくなる。
examples.english: If you overuse modifiers in writing, sentences become hard to understand.

notes:
A standard grammar term used in Japanese language education. Composed of {修飾|しゅうしょく} (modification, embellishment) + {語|ご} (word). In Japanese grammar education, modifiers are divided into two types.

TYPES OF MODIFIERS:
- {連体修飾語|れんたいしゅうしょくご}: adnominal modifier — modifies a noun (e.g., {赤|あか}い{花|はな}: red flower)
- {連用修飾語|れんようしゅうしょくご}: adverbial modifier — modifies a verb (e.g., ゆっくり{歩|ある}く: walk slowly)

RELATED WORDS:
- {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}: the word being modified
- {修飾|しゅうしょく}する: to modify
- {形容詞|けいようし}: adjective
- {副詞|ふくし}: adverb
- {連体詞|れんたいし}: pre-noun adjectival (Japanese-specific category)

USAGE:
This term is learned in Japanese elementary school {国語|こくご} (Japanese language) classes and continues through grammar study at all levels.
